title: Open detail D1c · Which button goes where in an “are you sure?” box
subtitle: From item 8; for Main's shared confirm box. Almost every box puts the button that changes nothing on the left (“Keep …”, focused first, so a stray Enter changes nothing) and the action on the right — red when it deletes. The three “… isn't saved” leave warnings (Color Belt's event and private grading, Star's grading; approved v0.192) do the reverse: “Leave anyway” on the left, “Stay on this page” on the right in blue, focused first (“nothing is deleted, so no red”). Forms' kiosk Open / End and Prospects' “Came?” focus the action first — they lose nothing, so that can stay. (Leave warning tested in the preview: one result set to fail to save, then Back · PC size · fake data)

row.caption: 1. Every delete box: “Keep …” on the left (focused first), the red action on the right.
2. The three leave warnings: “Leave anyway” on the left; blue “Stay on this page” on the right, focused first.

columns.label: Proposed (option B) · the same order everywhere

items.caption: 3. Option B: “Stay on this page” on the left (still focused first), “Leave anyway” on the right — red, because leaving loses the unsaved results for good (item 7).

columns.note: The rule in B: the button that changes nothing on the left; the action on the right — red when it loses something for good, blue otherwise; the first focus on the button that changes nothing whenever the action loses something, otherwise on the action (kiosk, “Came?”, as today). Picture 3 is drawn over the real box; nothing in the app was changed.

footer:
Your choice — one question: one button order in every box?
A · Keep as today. + no work; the leave warnings stay as approved (v0.192). − in three boxes the right-hand button means “stay” instead of “do it” — the reverse of every other box.
B · Recommended: the same order everywhere (picture 3). The leave warnings swap: “Stay on this page” left and focused, “Leave anyway” right and red. + right always does the thing, left always leaves things as they are; red always warns that something is lost for good. − three boxes change; v0.192 changes.
C · The same order, without the red: as B, but “Leave anyway” stays outline (v0.192's “no red”). + the order matches everywhere. − leaving loses results for good but doesn't look like it (against item 7's red rule).
